goal: Lets external mining software like Stratum v2's Job Declarator Server validate a block template it built itself, using the node's own mempool instead of a separate mirror mempool.
Removes redundant transaction storage and round trips for pool operators running SV2 job declaration.
reviewability: Paused because jeanpablojp asked on 2026-09-06 why makeTemplate() reports a different BIP-22 reason (stale-prevblk) than checkBlock() does for the same stale-prevblk case, and the author has not replied.
Several smaller doc nits from the same review are also unanswered but non-material.
agreement: Strong support from four reviewers with concept ACKs and no objections to the design (ismaelsadeeq, pablomartin4btc, enirox001, jeanpablojp).
enirox001 raised several implementation nits, all addressed by the author in pushes.
One open question about a reject-reason inconsistency from jeanpablojp is unanswered (jeanpablojp).

categories.name: mining
why: P2 because it gives external template builders (the Stratum v2 Job Declarator Server, and potentially a future p2pool weak-block validator) a way to validate transactions against the node's mempool without a mirror, removing real duplicated infrastructure that a working prototype already exercises.
It is a new capability rather than a fix to an existing template or acceptance bug, so it does not rise to P1.

result.summary: Adds a TxCollection interface to the Mining IPC surface that lets an external client (primarily the Stratum v2 Job Declarator Server) submit a list of wtxids, learn which are missing from the node's mempool, supply the missing transactions, and then have the node assemble and validate them into a block template. It also extracts a reusable CreateCoinbaseTx() helper from BlockAssembler::CreateNewBlock() and restricts several BlockTemplate methods (waitNext, getTxFees, getTxSigops, getCoinbaseTx) for externally generated templates since they don't apply.
result.problem: Stratum v2's Job Declarator Server currently keeps its own mirror of the node's mempool, populated by repeated getBlock()/waitNext() calls plus requests to the miner for anything missing, purely so it can validate externally proposed templates. This duplicates the node's mempool and adds bandwidth and maintenance overhead for pool operators running SV2 infrastructure.

open_concerns: jeanpablojp (2026-09-06): makeTemplate() labels an ancestor prevhash as 'stale-prevblk' while checkBlock()'s TestBlockValidity() path labels the same case 'inconclusive-not-best-prevblk'; asks whether the divergence from the described getblocktemplate-proposal convention was deliberate. Unanswered for 10 days.
jeanpablojp: suggests a test case for a coinbase whose witness commitment does not match the collected transactions (not yet added).
jeanpablojp: doc nits on missing @param/@returns and on what getCoinbaseTx() should say for external templates.
resolved_concerns: ViniciusCestarii's suggestion to split BlockTemplate into two capnp interfaces (narrow external one vs full one) instead of throwing on disallowed methods was discussed at length; author explained tradeoffs and both agreed it's a judgment call, not blocking ('I'm fine either way' - ViniciusCestarii).

pablomartin4btc's and enirox001's numerous implementation nits (duplicate wtxid check ordering, mutex scope, reserve() before mempool lock, Assert vs Assume, naming m_collected_txs -> m_tx_collection, missing size check before mempool loop) were all addressed by the author in the 2026-08-20 push.

enirox001's concern about the intra-commit sequencing of the 'make TxCollection create a BlockTemplate' vs 'restrict externally generated templates' commits was declined by the author ('I'd rather not grow the commit... commits are bisect-safe'), with no pushback.

categories.name: ipc
categories.evidence: The PR adds a new capnp interface (TxCollection) and Mining method, but the subject is what the mining interface exposes to external template builders, not IPC serialization, connection handling, or the capnp toolchain itself. Per the category's exclusion rule, a mining interface extension is ipc only when the interface mechanics are the point, which is not the case here.
categories.rationale: Not a member: no IPC-label, and the change is scoped to what the Mining interface offers rather than to IPC infrastructure mechanics.

categories.name: mining
categories.evidence: Labeled Mining; adds a new interfaces::Mining method (collectTxs) and TxCollection interface, extracts BlockAssembler::CreateCoinbaseTx(), and restricts BlockTemplate methods for externally generated templates, all core mining-interface subject matter with the SV2 Job Declarator Server as the demonstrated consumer.
categories.rationale: P2 because it gives the Stratum v2 Job Declarator Server (and potentially future p2pool weak-block validation) a way to validate externally built templates against the node's real mempool, eliminating a duplicated mirror mempool; a working consumer prototype exists (stratum-mining/sv2-apps#599). It is new capability rather than a fix for a template-invalidity or acceptance bug, so it does not reach P1, but multiple reviewers treat it as a durable architectural improvement worth deliberate review (enirox001: 'the main benefit is architectural...').

Whether the project intends TxCollection primarily as a stepping stone toward p2pool/compact-block reuse (raised speculatively by the author) or purely as an SV2 JDS feature, which would affect how much leverage to credit.
